# `sim/physics/PhysicsSchema.js`

> **Source:** `engine/sim/physics/PhysicsSchema.js`

PhysicsSchema.js - Unified JSON Schema for Physics System Defines consistent data structures for: - Body types (dynamic, kinematic, static) - Collider shapes (box, sphere, capsule, mesh) - Joint types (D6, revolute, spherical, distance) - Collision layers and masks - Material properties (friction, restitution) All physics code should use these schemas for consistency.

## Functions

### `getSimModeId(modeName)`

Get simulation mode ID from name

### `getSimModeName(modeId)`

Get simulation mode name from ID

### `getColliderShapeId(shapeName)`

Get collider shape ID from name

### `getColliderShapeName(shapeId)`

Get collider shape name from ID

### `getCollisionMask(...layerNames)`

Get collision layer mask from layer names

### `layersCollide(maskA, maskB)`

Check if two layer masks collide

### `validatePhysicsBody(config)`

Validate physics body configuration

### `validateCollider(config)`

Validate collider configuration

### `validatePhysicsMaterial(config)`

Validate physics material

### `createDefaultPhysicsBody()`

Create default physics body config

### `createDefaultCollider(shape = "box")`

Create default collider config

### `createDefaultJoint(type = "fixed")`

Create default joint config

### `createDefaultPhysicsWorld()`

Create default physics world config

### `getPhysicsMaterial(name)`

Get physics material by name

## Constants

- `SIM_MODES` — Physics simulation modes
- `COLLIDER_SHAPES` — Collider shape types
- `JOINT_TYPES` — Joint types for articulated bodies
- `D6_MOTION` — D6 joint axis motion types
- `D6_AXES` — D6 joint axes
- `D6_DRIVES`
- `COLLISION_LAYERS` — Collision layer definitions (bitmask)
- `PHYSICS_MATERIAL_SCHEMA` — Physics material schema **Compliant Contacts (PhysX 5.1+):** Set restitution to a NEGATIVE value to enable spring-damper contact model. This provides more stable collision behavior for complex contact configurations. - restitution = -springStiffness (negative enables compliant mode) - damping = damping ratio for the spring - compliantAcceleration = true to use acceleration spring (mass-independent)
- `PHYSICS_MATERIALS` — Preset physics materials Note: Negative restitution enables compliant (spring-damper) contacts
- `PHYSICS_BODY_SCHEMA` — Physics body schema
- `COLLIDER_SCHEMA` — Collider schema
- `JOINT_SCHEMA` — Joint schema
- `PHYSICS_WORLD_SCHEMA` — Physics world configuration
- `STANDARD_COLLIDER_MESHES` — Standard convex collider mesh IDs

## Notes & Examples

### Physics Engine Integration

The physics system provides rigid body dynamics, collision detection, and raycasting. Bodies have shapes (box, sphere, mesh), mass properties, and constraints. The GPU physics engine accelerates broad-phase collision detection and particle systems.

**Example: Creating physics bodies**
```js
import { PhysicsWorld } from 'engine/physics/PhysicsWorld.js';
import { RigidBody } from 'engine/physics/RigidBody.js';
import { BoxShape, SphereShape } from 'engine/physics/Shapes.js';

const world = new PhysicsWorld({ gravity: [0, -9.8, 0] });

// Static ground
const ground = new RigidBody({
  type: 'static',
  shape: new BoxShape(10, 1, 10),
  position: [0, -0.5, 0]
});
world.addBody(ground);

// Dynamic box
const box = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  mass: 1,
  shape: new BoxShape(1, 1, 1),
  position: [0, 5, 0],
  restitution: 0.5  // Bounciness
});
world.addBody(box);
```

**Advanced: Collision detection and raycasting**
```js
// Raycast to find what the player is looking at
const hit = world.raycast(camera.position, camera.forward, 100);
if (hit) {
  console.log('Hit entity:', hit.body.entityId);
  console.log('Hit point:', hit.point);
  console.log('Hit normal:', hit.normal);
  
  // Apply impulse at hit point
  hit.body.applyImpulse([0, 10, 0], hit.point);
}

// Shapecast (swept sphere) for character movement
const sweep = world.shapecast(
  player.position,           // Start
  desiredPosition,           // End
  new SphereShape(0.5),    // Player capsule radius
  { ignore: player.body }  // Don't collide with self
);
if (sweep.hit) {
  // Slide along wall
  player.position = sweep.position;
}
```

**Advanced: Constraints and joints**
```js
import { HingeConstraint, FixedConstraint } from 'engine/physics/Constraints.js';

// Door hinge
const doorHinge = new HingeConstraint({
  bodyA: doorFrame,
  bodyB: door,
  pivot: [0, 1, 0],      // Hinge location
  axis: [0, 1, 0],       // Hinge axis (Y up)
  limits: [-90, 90]      // Open angle range in degrees
});
world.addConstraint(doorHinge);

// Ragdoll joint (ball-and-socket)
const shoulder = new FixedConstraint({
  bodyA: torso,
  bodyB: arm,
  pivotA: [0.5, 1.5, 0],  // Shoulder position on torso
  pivotB: [0, 0, 0]       // Shoulder position on arm
});
world.addConstraint(shoulder);
```

**Advanced: Continuous collision detection (CCD)**
```js
// Fast-moving objects need CCD to not tunnel through walls
const projectile = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  shape: new SphereShape(0.1),
  mass: 0.1,
  ccd: { enabled: true, sweptSphereRadius: 0.1 },
  linearDamping: 0  // No air resistance for bullets
});
projectile.velocity = [0, 0, 100];  // Very fast
world.addBody(projectile);
```

**Gotchas:**
- **Units**: Physics uses meters, kilograms, seconds. A 1-unit cube is 1 meter.
- **Time step**: Fixed time step (1/60) gives stable simulation; variable dt causes explosions.
- **Collision layers**: Use collision masks to filter what collides (player vs enemy, bullet vs world).
- **Sleeping**: At-rest bodies sleep to save CPU — wake them before applying forces.
